lead: A single force can be replaced by two or more forces that add to it. That replacement is resolution. The reverse, composition, rebuilds one force from several. Engineers resolve a slanted force into horizontal and vertical parts because those parts enter equilibrium equations separately. They compose a set of pulls into one resultant. The same idea handles a rope tension, a wind load on a hoarding, or a crane cable, and it is the first calculation step in most statics problems.
prereq: You need: Chapter 1.2 for vector components, unit vectors and the dot product.

blocks.text: Take a force F of 50 N at θ = 30° from the positive x-axis. Drop a perpendicular from the tip of the arrow to each axis. The two perpendicular sides are the rectangular components. They replace the original force exactly, because their vector sum returns F.
F<sub>x</sub> = F cos θ,   F<sub>y</sub> = F sin θ
blocks.where: F is the force magnitude in N; θ is the angle from the positive x-axis, measured counterclockwise; F<sub>x</sub> and F<sub>y</sub> are signed components in N.

blocks.text: θ is measured counterclockwise from +x. In quadrant I both signs are positive. In quadrant II x is negative and y positive. In quadrant III both negative. In quadrant IV x positive and y negative. Decide the signs from the sketch before you substitute. Do not let the calculator choose for you.

items: Draw the force arrow and mark θ from the positive x-axis.
Write the signs for the quadrant on the sketch: I (+,+), II (−,+), III (−,−), IV (+,−).
Substitute F<sub>x</sub> = F cos θ and F<sub>y</sub> = F sin θ with those signs.

blocks.text: A force of 50 N at 30° gives F<sub>x</sub> = 50 cos 30° = 43.3 N and F<sub>y</sub> = 50 sin 30° = 25.0 N. A force of 50 N at 150° gives F<sub>x</sub> = −43.3 N and F<sub>y</sub> = +25.0 N. The magnitude is still 50 N.

sections.h3: Oblique resolution with the sine rule

blocks.text: Two chosen directions need not be at right angles. Suppose a force F is to be split along line a and line b. Draw F as one side of a triangle. Draw the two components P and Q as the other sides. The triangle closes, so the sine rule applies.

The angle opposite P is the angle between F and line b. The angle opposite Q is the angle between F and line a. The angle opposite F is the angle between the two chosen lines. Use magnitudes; put the negative sign back if a component must point opposite its chosen arrow.
P / sin γ = Q / sin β = F / sin α
blocks.where: F is the force being resolved in N; P is the component along line a; Q is along line b; α is the angle between lines a and b; β is the angle between F and line a; γ is the angle between F and line b.

blocks.text: In the worked example the force is at 30°, the chosen lines are at 0° and 75°, so β = 30°, γ = 45°, α = 75°. The sine rule then gives P = 36.6 N and Q = 25.9 N.
Composition is the reverse. Two forces P and Q act at a point with angle α between their directions. Complete the parallelogram. The diagonal from the point is the resultant R.

blocks.where: P and Q are the two forces in N; α is the angle between their directions; R is the resultant magnitude in N.

blocks.text: tan θ = Q sin α / (P + Q cos α)
blocks.where: θ is the angle from P toward Q; P, Q, α are as above.

blocks.text: The formula uses the angle between P and Q, not the angle between R and either force. Many wrong answers come from that swap. Check the special cases in the table.
Some syllabi call composition the resultant of two forces and resolution splitting a force into components. For three or more forces, add components instead; see Chapter 1.4.

figure.caption: The two curves show the horizontal and vertical components of a 50 N force as θ turns through a full circle. At θ = 30° they read 43.3 N and 25.0 N, matching the worked example.

spec.aria: Two curves show the horizontal and vertical components of a 50 N force as its angle turns through a full circle; each component peaks at 50 N and falls to zero or −50 N a quarter turn later.

examples.question: A force of 50 N acts at 30° above the horizontal. (a) Resolve it into horizontal and vertical components. (b) Resolve the same force along the horizontal and along a line at 75° above the horizontal.
steps: (a) Take θ = 30° from the positive x-axis. The horizontal component is F<sub>x</sub> = 50 cos 30°.
The vertical component is F<sub>y</sub> = 50 sin 30°. sin 30° = 0.5000, so F<sub>y</sub> = 50 × 0.5000 = 25.0 N.
(b) The chosen directions are 0° and 75°. The force is at 30°. Angle between F and horizontal = 30°. Angle between F and 75° line = 45°. Angle between the two chosen lines = 75°.
In the force triangle: P (horizontal) is opposite 45°, Q (along 75°) is opposite 30°, and F = 50 N is opposite 75°.
Sine rule: P / sin 45° = Q / sin 30° = 50 / sin 75°.
Check in rectangular form: 36.6i + 25.9(cos 75° i + sin 75° j) = (36.6 + 6.70)i + 25.0j = 43.3i + 25.0j N.
examples.answer: F<sub>x</sub> = 43.3 N, F<sub>y</sub> = 25.0 N; and along the chosen lines P = 36.6 N horizontal and Q = 25.9 N at 75°.
examples.check:
import math
F=50
th=math.radians(30)
Fx=F*math.cos(th)
Fy=F*math.sin(th)
P=F*math.sin(math.radians(45))/math.sin(math.radians(75))
Q=F*math.sin(math.radians(30))/math.sin(math.radians(75))
print(round(Fx,1))
print(round(Fy,1))
print(round(P,1))
print(round(Q,1))

traps: If θ is measured from the vertical, the horizontal part is F sin θ and the vertical part is F cos θ. Do not copy F cos θ for x without checking where θ starts.
Dropping the minus sign in quadrants II or III. A force of 50 N at 150° has F<sub>x</sub> = −43.3 N, not +43.3 N.
In oblique resolution, putting an angle in the wrong place of the sine rule. Label the side opposite each angle before dividing.
Using the angle between R and P instead of the angle between P and Q in the parallelogram formula. α is between the two forces.
Using tan θ = Q sin α/(P + Q cos α) but reporting θ from Q. θ is measured from P toward Q.

quiz.q: Define resolution and composition of a force.
quiz.a: Resolution replaces one force by two or more forces whose vector sum is the original. Composition replaces two or more forces by one resultant force.

quiz.q: Write F<sub>x</sub> and F<sub>y</sub> for a force F at angle θ from +x.
quiz.a: F<sub>x</sub> = F cos θ and F<sub>y</sub> = F sin θ; θ is counterclockwise from +x, and signs come from the quadrant.

quiz.q: Why is F<sub>x</sub> negative at θ = 150° even though cos 150° is calculated from a positive F?
quiz.a: The angle puts the force in quadrant II. The x component points left, so the signed value is F cos 150° = −0.866F. The magnitude is 0.866F; the negative sign shows direction.

quiz.q: An 80 N force acts at 120° from +x. Find its rectangular components.
Two forces 30 N and 40 N act at 60° to each other. Find R and θ from the 30 N force.
Using R = √(P² + Q² + 2PQ cos α), explain why R is largest at α = 0° and smallest at α = 180°.
quiz.a: cos α is +1 at 0°, so R² = (P + Q)². cos α is −1 at 180°, so R² = (P − Q)². In between cos α falls, so R falls from P + Q to |P − Q|.

quiz.q: A force is resolved into two perpendicular components 43.3 N and 25.0 N. Find the original magnitude and angle from +x.
In the worked example, why is P only 36.6 N when the horizontal component of the 50 N force is 43.3 N?
quiz.a: The second component Q also has a horizontal part. Q cos 75° = 25.9 × 0.2588 = 6.7 N. P plus that part gives 36.6 + 6.7 = 43.3 N.

beyond: Not for the exam. Robotics and game engines store forces as Cartesian components and use rotation matrices to resolve them into new axes. Finite element software resolves loads along element local axes for every member. Surveying and navigation use the same sine-rule triangle when two bearings fix a point. Search for vector components, parallelogram law of forces and oblique resolution sine rule.
